To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The learning curve for LRP in our centre was 50 cases; 2) The complication rate was low and comparable to the published literature; 3) The oncological outcome was excellent; 4) There was a significant increase in operative time during the learning curve; 5) The operative time decreased significantly with the introduction of a standardized approach to LRP.
The first 50 cases of laparoscopic prostatectomies in our centre showed a steep learning curve.

the following questions: (1) How many cases are required for a surgeon to achieve a low complication rate?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LRP is a technically demanding and challenging procedure, and that the learning curve is steep.
the LRP is a safe and feasible operation for appropriately selected patients, and the Fellowship training is a valuable and important adjunct to the learning curve.
LRP is safe and feasible and should be offered to patients with localized prostate cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the introduction of a training program has improved the outcome of the first 50 cases of LRP in our centre.
we are now able to perform LRP with acceptable operative time, blood loss, complications, and continence and potency outcomes, with the added benefit of training a Fellow.
LRP is safe, feasible and can be performed with a low rate of complications and acceptable cancer control.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the learning curve for LRP is steep and that a dedicated training programme is necessary to achieve proficiency.
the introduction of a training program during the first 50 cases of LRP is feasible and safe.
LRP can be performed safely and effectively by a single surgeon with no prior robotic experience, with the assistance of a surgical fellow.
